rows.title: Performance Comparison of API Protocols: A Systematic Review of REST, GRPC and Graph QL
rows.venue: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering Management & Applied Science
rows.authors: Munir Ali Mohammed; Shra Fatima; Ajaz Husain Warsi
rows.abstract: The correct choice of API protocols in the modern distributed systems defines the level of performance, scalability, and resource efficiency. The current paper contains a systematic literature review (SLR) of 20 empirical studies in total published in 2020-2025 by comparing the top three architectural styles, namely, REST, gRPC, and GraphQL. This review offers a review of the evidence-based framework of protocol selection by synthesizing data on latency, throughput, resource utilization, and scalability. rows.title: A Comparative Design Study of REST, GraphQL and gRPC APIs for Large-Scale Applications
rows.venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
rows.abstract: Aim. This study aims to comparatively analyze REST, GraphQL, and gRPC API paradigms to guide architectural decision-making in large-scale, distributed applications. It focuses on understanding how each paradigm addresses scalability, performance, and maintainability challenges. The goal is to provide practical insights for system architects. Emphasis is placed on real-world constraints such as latency, data consistency, and team productivity. The study targets enterprise and cloud-native systems. rows.venue: International Journal of Emerging Research in Engineering and Technology
rows.abstract: This study provides a thorough performance comparison that assesses three commonly utilized API transmission protocols REST, GraphQL, along with Grpc against critical metrics that include latency, payload speed of throughput, and scalability. The purpose is for providing system architects and developers a meaningful understanding of how each system protocol works with different types of workloads and in what cases. rows.venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
rows.authors: G. Swapna; S. V. Punith Kumar; E. Susmitha
rows.abstract: Microservice-based architectures require efficient communication mechanisms to ensure high performance and scalability. REST, which relies on HTTP/1.1 and JSON, is widely adopted due to its simplicity but suffers from larger payload sizes and higher latency. In contrast, gRPC utilizes HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers, enabling faster communication through binary serialization and persistent connections. rows.title: A performance comparison of web programming interfaces: GraphQL, gRPC and Thrift
rows.abstract: This article presents a comparative performance comparison of three technologies commonly used to implement web programming interfaces: GraphQL, gRPC and Thrift. For the purposes of this study, three applications were developed, each utilizing one of the selected technologies. The applications were tested using JMeter. The execution time and data volume returned during operations performed on a relational database were measured. rows.title: Comparative Performance Analysis of GRPC and Rest API Under Various Traffic Conditions and Data Sizes Using a Quantitative Approach
rows.venue: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
rows.authors: Moch. Zukhruf Ain; Rizka Ardiansyah; Septiano Anggun Pratama; Muhammad Akbar
rows.abstract: Web 3.0 presents challenges in efficient data exchange, especially in decentralized systems. REST API (HTTP/1.1) remains widely used due to its broad compatibility but has communication inefficiencies, while gRPC (HTTP/2) offers better performance with multiplexing and Protocol Buffers. This study compares REST API and gRPC under various traffic conditions and data sizes using Apache JMeter and Wireshark, measuring throughput, response time, latency, and data transfer efficiency. rows.venue: International journal of Computer Networks & Communications
rows.authors: Hari Krishna S M; Rinki Sharma
rows.abstract: Cloud computing is the quick, simple, and economical distribution of computing services. rows.title: Architectural Patterns for Building Secure High-Load APIs on Node.js Using REST, gRPC, and GraphQL
rows.venue: International Journal of Engineering in Computer Science
rows.abstract: The article examines the architecture of secure and high-load APIs developed with the Node.js platform and the REST, gRPC, and GraphQL technologies. The importance of selecting an appropriate interaction model based on load context and security requirements is emphasized. rows.venue: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University Technical sciences
rows.abstract: The microservice architectural pattern has rapidly emerged as a dominant and highly effective approach for building complex, distributed, and scalable applications in modern software engineering.
